dataAnomalies.implication: Unusual service offering for a fuel station; likely a database error or a legacy COVID-era offering that is no longer active.
dataAnomalies.sourceQuote: The "Oxygen" Anomaly: One data source mentions "Oxygen Filling Services". This is highly unusual for a retail fuel outlet. It is assessed to be either a database error conflating the entity with an industrial gas supplier or a remnant of a temporary facility established during the COVID-19 pandemic (2020-2021) when many industrial units in the Narela/Alipur belt pivoted to oxygen handling. For the purpose of current asset valuation, this should be treated as a non-core or legacy data point.

dataAnomalies.dataPoint: Normal petrol not available at 9:00 PM
dataAnomalies.implication: Indicates potential inventory management issues or a deliberate strategy to push higher-margin branded fuel, leading to customer dissatisfaction.
dataAnomalies.sourceQuote: The "Availability" Crisis: A review explicitly mentions "normal petrol not available at 9:00 PM". In fuel retail, stock-outs are a critical failure. They suggest either poor inventory planning (working capital constraints) or a deliberate strategy to push higher-margin "Speed" (branded petrol) by claiming normal fuel is out of stock—a practice that irritates customers and damages trust.

dataAnomalies.dataPoint: Reviews questioning the quantity of fuel dispensed
dataAnomalies.implication: Raises concerns about dispensing accuracy and customer trust, suggesting a need for regular calibration checks.
dataAnomalies.sourceQuote: The "Quantity" Anxiety: Reviews questioning the quantity of fuel dispensed strike at the core of the business's integrity. While often perception-based, failing to address these with visible calibration checks (using the 5-liter standard measure) allows the narrative of "theft" to fester.
